anita: FYI - noticed ~12% p99 host-ingress latency bump after the kernel-selector tweak merged last night :warning:

mike: which tweak exactly? stack or batch heuristic?

anita: it was the heuristic that prefers larger 'combined' kernel paths for mid-length sequences. seemed fine in unit tests but production shows extra work in preparse/tokenize stage. attaching quick flame.

anita: ```
preparse: median 4.2ms -> 4.6ms
preparse p99: 12.1ms -> 13.5ms
grpc smallwrites/sec +18%
http2 frames <1kb +27%
kv_cache miss rate +9%
```

liz: seeing matching signal on proxy - more tiny frames, writev coalescing disabled on canary? that will amplify syscalls.

raj: curious about kv miss spike. kernel selection changed sequence length grouping, keys might be different (prefixes + length bin) -> more shard flips and cold misses.

nick: quick options: revert selector, or ship microfix: 1) reduce preparse combined-batch threshold 2) enable writev coalesce on proxy 3) bump preparse threadpool from 4->8 for canary.

mike: +1 revert if easy. but if rollback risky, let's try writev + threadpool first (lower blast).

anita: created short runbook, running canary with writev on eu-west and +2 threads on host-preparse. will also add kv hit counters to tracing.

liz: config snippet (proxy): ```yaml
writev_coalesce: true
coalesce_threshold_bytes: 4096
max_coalesce_count: 8
```

raj: for kv: consider normalizing keying to ignore kernel-bucket id or use stable shard hashing to avoid unnecessary re-routing. small experiment: set kv_shard_stable: true for canary.

nick: also check streaming chunker: the new combined path emits smaller early chunks; we can bump min-chunk-size to avoid extra HTTP/2 frames.

anita: smoke after canary start: p50 unchanged, p95 down slightly, p99 back to -4% vs baseline in eu-west with writev+threads enabled :thumbsup: will roll to us-east next.

deploy-bot: canary deploy completed: host-preparse+proxy-writev canary -> eu-west-1 @1748808210

mike: nice. follow-up: add perf test to CI that simulates many short chat messages to catch this class of regressions.

anita: filing follow-up ticket with perf diffs and proposed kernel-selector tuning. will hold off on full revert until we try selector tuning + kv normalization.

liz: thanks everyone - great quick triage. emoji reactions :rocket:
